recipe.title: Caramel Pecan Cottage Cheese Bowl
recipe.summary: Creamy cottage cheese topped with candied pecans, sugar-free caramel, and chunks of a white chocolate-coated pumpkin cookie protein bar.
recipe.story: Savory cottage cheese and sweet caramel play off each other here, with cut chunks of a Built Puff bar adding crunch, a white chocolate shell, and a fudgy pumpkin-cookie center for the season.
ingredients: 1 tablespoon Splenda brown sugar blend (optional, for candying the pecans)
1 Built Puff Pumpkin Cookie Chunk bar, cut into bite-size chunks
instructions: Optional upgrade: toss the chopped pecans with the Splenda brown sugar blend in a small microwave-safe bowl and microwave for 30 to 45 seconds, stirring halfway, until fragrant. Let cool for 1 minute so they crisp up.
Scoop the cottage cheese into a bowl and sprinkle with the cinnamon.
Top with the pecans (candied or plain), drizzle with the sugar-free caramel sauce, and finish with the Built Puff bar chunks.
Serve right away for the best crunch.
tips: Short on time? Skip the candying step — plain chopped pecans still taste great here.
Cut the Built Puff bar into chunks just before serving so the white chocolate coating stays crisp instead of softening in the fridge.
Warm the caramel sauce for about 10 seconds if you want it extra drizzly.

images.image_prompt: Premium food-blog photo of a bowl of plain creamy white cottage cheese. On one side of the bowl, a small pile of dark caramel-glazed candied pecan pieces, deep amber-brown in color. On the other side of the bowl, separate and not touching the caramel or pecans, 4 to 5 irregular cut chunks of a protein bar. CRITICAL: the outside surface of every bar chunk is coated in solid, opaque, bright WHITE chocolate -- like a white candy shell, the color of white chocolate or white icing. The white coating must stay completely clean, matte, and pale -- it must NOT be brown, tan, toasted, golden, glazed, or caramel-colored, and must NOT resemble a crouton, a cube of bread, granola, or a toasted cookie. One bar chunk lies on its side to reveal a freshly cut cross-section: the interior is a solid, deeply saturated pumpkin-orange color, like pureed pumpkin or sweet potato, fudgy and moist-looking, with tiny darker brown flecks of cinnamon cookie dough mixed through it. The contrast between the white outer shell and the orange interior must be obvious and high-contrast, like a white-shelled candy with orange filling. A light drizzle of sugar-free caramel sauce touches only the cottage cheese and pecans, never the white bar chunks. Warm amber fall light, rust linen napkin, natural wood surface, no fruit or extra garnish, no text overlay.
